messages:
Kim P: Heads up — inference-rate alert (INF_RATE_01) for the new model canary is spiking during rollout. It's noisy and drowning out the real pages. Can we schedule a short mute while we finish the canary? Thinking 30m.
Olga R: Which dashboard / query should we check before muting? want to confirm this is rollout-related and not a regression. link?
Kim P: dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/infra/inference/rate?range=15m — focus on node/gpu-pool-2 and model:open-release-v2. Spikes correlate with the canary tasks starting at ~1812345000.
Mike L: If it's rollout traffic pattern, a short mute is fine. Alternative is to bump threshold to p95>120rps for 30m, but mute is simplest.
Olga R: Can you include the exact mute command you want executed and the reason so oncall can approve quickly? Also add a runbook link.
Kim P: sure — command we use: ```srectl alerts mute --id=INF_RATE_01 --for=30m --by=kim.p --reason="canary rollout: open-release-v2" --annotation="canary:open-release-v2; rollout-id=canary-2026-03-17"``` runbook: https://wiki.redwood.ai/runbooks/inference-rate
deploy-bot: Canary rollout started for open-release-v2 on cluster gpu-pool-2 (canary-2026-03-17). Tickets: RD-4321 :shipit:
Olga R: @sre-oncall can you approve a 30m snooze for INF_RATE_01? we'll annotate and monitor, will revert if weird patterns continue.
sre-oncall: Approved. Muting INF_RATE_01 for 30 minutes starting now. Annotation: "canary rollout: open-release-v2 by Kim P". I will set a reminder to re-evaluate at end of mute window. :white_check_mark:
Mike L: :thumbsup: please post any notable changes in token-level latency or error-rate in this thread as you see them.
Kim P: will do. initial check: p95 latency unchanged, error-rate steady. thanks all for quick response.
Olga R: leaving a note in the alert config: consider adjusting sensitivity during rolling deploys — maybe a short default cooldown for pipeline deployments. filing follow-up RD-4377.
Kim P: thanks — closing the loop here, will post another update before the mute expires.
